parts:
On 15 Jun 2016, at 13:39, Michael Kunst wrote:

> I ust wanted again to say how great it was meeting you, it really
> helped me a lot in thinking about the future of my project. I also
> delved a bit more into the nat package. I already figured out how to
> rescale the dimension of my tracing and how to apply my registration
> to my tracings as well.

Super!

> I’m currently in the process of generating a template brain and
> wanted to know what you used to make the associated .surf file. I
> assume it was Amira.

Yes

> We do not have an Amira license, can I just use FluoRender or ImageJ
> to generate this file?

I believe that you can do this in both programs, although I have not
tried. With ImageJ google offered this:

http://132.187.25.13/ij3d/?category=Extensions&page=Create_Surfaces

The plugin mentioned may already be included in Fiji. There is also a
tool called ITK SNAP used a lot in human brain imaging that should be
good.

We have ways write now to import amira hxurf, obj or ply format into R.
I can provide specific details depending on what output format you end
up with. Meshlab is a useful software for looking at / editing /
converting surface meshes.

Best,

Greg.
